subject: SLA template: uptime floor, latency targets and monthly credit workplan
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@cycloneai.com>
To: alex.martinez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cycloneai.com
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA ask: uptime floor + monthly credits (follow-up)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we discussed, our production traffic for inference is highly bursty during weekend promotions and has strict p95 latency requirements for user-facing requests. Procurement asked me to follow up with a concrete ask so they can compare the SLA to our internal procurement guardrails.

Key asks from our side: 
- Uptime baseline: 99.7% (we understand historical availability at the model level; we need a firm floor for financial planning)
- Latency: p95 < 300ms for our routed model variant (we can accept a degraded p95 for cold-start windows)
- Monthly credits: simple, predictable schedule and a cap for litigation/credit accounting.
- Maintenance carveouts: we need clarity on what counts as planned maintenance and a 30-day advance notice requirement.

We are open to a phased approach. Ideally, procurement would like to see an initial 90-day pilot where credits are capped at 10% of monthly invoice, then re-evaluate. Can you share Redwood's standard template and any options for temporary exception windows for bursty workloads?

Appreciate a quick outline and if you can copy your billing/CS contacts.

Best,
Nina Patel
Head of Procurement, CycloneAI
procurement@cycloneai.com
attachments: cycloneai-operational-summary.xlsx (spreadsheet, 82KB)

From: alex.martinez@redwood.com
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@cycloneai.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask: uptime floor + monthly credits (follow-up)

Hi Nina —

Thanks for the clear ask and the traffic summary (received). Attaching our SLA template v2 for reference — the key items below are a starting point and we can mark sections as "pilot exceptions" if you prefer a time-boxed approach.

Proposal (high level):
- Standard uptime baseline: 99.9% (hosted). For CycloneAI we can offer a provisional floor of 99.7% for the first 90 days as a pilot, subject to monthly review.
- Latency target: p95 < 300ms for the primary routed variant; during cold starts we allow a 2x degradation window up to 120s for the first 5 minutes of a scaled pod spin-up (we'll provide metrics and dashboard hooks).
- Credits: monthly credit table tiered by monthly uptime percentage: 
  * >=99.9%: no credit
  * 99.5% - 99.9%: 10% of monthly invoice
  * 99.0% - 99.5%: 25% of monthly invoice
  * <99.0%: 50% of monthly invoice (capped at annual maximum equal to 3x monthly invoice)
- For the 90-day pilot we can cap monthly credits at 10% as you requested and include an operational buffer that prevents triggering credits for transient platform spin events under 5 minutes.
- Maintenance carveouts: planned maintenance with 30-day notice is excluded; emergency maintenance will be posted with a post-mortem. We propose a quarterly maintenance window schedule to minimize surprise.

Next steps: if the above is acceptable as a baseline, I'll loop in Marissa (CS) to scope the dashboard hooks and Ben (Billing) to draft the credit cap language for your procurement team.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call.

Alex Martinez
Sales, Redwood Inference
Alex.Martinez@redwood.com
attachments: redwood-sla-template-v2.pdf (PDF, 45KB)

Marissa here — product/legal notes below (high level):
- Product: need to confirm the cold-start carveout details and the exact signal for "pod spin" events. Also request example traffic traces from CycloneAI to validate the 5-minute buffer assumption.
- Legal: prefers a fixed credit cap (we should propose 3x monthly invoice annual cap as Alex suggested) and would like to restrict credits to service downtime, not broader business impact claims.

Ben — can you draft the credit clause and the exact phrasing for the 90-day pilot cap (10%)? Also confirm billing procedures for applying credits (automated invoice credit vs future invoice reconciliation).

Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@cycloneai.com>, alex.martinez@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask: uptime floor + monthly credits (follow-up)

Hi Nina —

Thanks for the clear framing. We can proceed with the 90-day pilot as proposed. Quick notes on the credit mechanics: 
- For the pilot period we will cap monthly credits at 10% of the monthly invoice. Credits will be applied as an automated invoice credit in the month following the incident once the incident and root cause are verified.
- For the long-term SLA (post-pilot) we'll move to the tiered credit table Alex outlined with an annual cap equal to 3x the typical monthly invoice.
- We'll add explicit language that only platform service availability and token-serving latency are eligible for credits; integrations, customer-side misconfigurations, and third-party network outages are excluded.

I'll prepare a short amendment paragraph to insert into the SLA template and share a tracked version by EOD tomorrow. If procurement is fine with the 30-day planned maintenance notice and the 5-minute transient buffer, we can have a redlined SLA for signature within the next week.

Ben Carter
Billing & Contracts, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
